title: Exercise 7A · Q9(d)
summary: The height BD makes two right-angled triangles: find AD and DC, then add.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q9(d): In the figure, BD ⊥ AC, BD = 24 cm, AB = 30 cm and BC = 26 cm. Find the value of d, the length of AC.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In the figure, **BD ⊥ AC**. **BD = 24 cm**, **AB = 30 cm** and **BC = 26 cm**. We have to find **d**, the length of **AC**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔABD, **∠D = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AB**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{AD^2} \\ \role{legB}{AD^2} &= \role{hyp}{AB^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{AD^2} \\ \role{legB}{AD^2} &= \role{hyp}{AB^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{30^2} - \role{legA}{24^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{900} - \role{legA}{576} \\ &= \role{legB}{324}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{AD^2} \\ \role{legB}{AD^2} &= \role{hyp}{AB^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{30^2} - \role{legA}{24^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{900} - \role{legA}{576} \\ &= \role{legB}{324} \\ \role{legB}{AD} &= \sqrt{324} = 18\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔCBD, **∠D = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **BC**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BC^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{DC^2} \\ \role{legB}{DC^2} &= \role{hyp}{BC^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BC^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{DC^2} \\ \role{legB}{DC^2} &= \role{hyp}{BC^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{26^2} - \role{legA}{24^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{676} - \role{legA}{576} \\ &= \role{legB}{100}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BC^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{DC^2} \\ \role{legB}{DC^2} &= \role{hyp}{BC^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{26^2} - \role{legA}{24^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{676} - \role{legA}{576} \\ &= \role{legB}{100} \\ \role{legB}{DC} &= \sqrt{100} = 10\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Add the two parts
steps.narration: **AC** is made of **AD** and **DC**.\[\begin{aligned}d = AC &= AD + DC \\ &= 18 + 10 \\ &= \role{ans}{28\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check DC
challenges.prompt: In ΔCBD, BC = 26 cm and BD = 24 cm. Find **DC**.

takeaways: Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.
